title: Oomb,
html_source:
As Stephen kisses the ghost, the death-mother pulls him back through her womb, through the Earth, and to the darkness of the evening sky. The intensity of the pull back to the mother causes Stephen to lose control to speak rationally and what issues from his mouth is a primal yell that is the “roar of cataractic planets, globed, blazing, roaring wayawayawayawayawayaway.” He has gone so far in to the darkness of the universe that he has felt blinded. When he regains thought, he turns his back to the sun and begins scribbling words, which are likely related to the experience he has just had of the death-mother. Stephen’s controlled experience of blindness at the chapter’s beginning culminates in this experience of mother consciousness which ends in cosmic darkness. Where before he thought of the limits of the diaphane and adiaphane, he has now perceived them through direct perception.
Feeling constrained by limits, he wonders why he may not transcend them. He has found, through the lens of Aristotle, less translucence in his body than he has found darkness. The experience of the death-mother leads Stephen to suggest that darkness is in the soul, which holds all of one’s psychic events, but is most damaged by one’s “sins.” The experience can be read also as Stephen’s union with the mem-aleph which constitutes the primary mother syllable, MA, and has acted as the force of feminine wisdom behind his desire to write the alphabet books.

PROPOSED SUGGESTION: Any further reading on this analysis? I’m interested.
